text:
jamal: Heads-up — during the heuristics-ramp A/B this morning we saw a ~3-4s p95 jump on the 'fast-path' kernels for short seqs. started ~09:02 UTC and lasted ~6m.
alex: saw that on the latency dashboard too, weird mismatch between request count and kernel selection logs. requests still routed to fast-path but CPU flips to >90%.
maria: any obvious config changes rolled out? batching heuristics tweak yesterday morning but should be gated.
linh: no infra deploys around that time, only an experiment ramp for batch-window=8->6 that started 08:55. I rolled it back at 09:10.
jamal: attaching the short trace sample where spans are missing after sampler drop — looks like our trace-sampler dropped spans for the kernel switch.
jamal: ```
# trace snippet (sanitized)
span: request/serve start
span: batching/schedule
# missing: kernel/select and runtime/exec spans for ~120 requests
span: response/send
```
alex: interesting — logs show kernel selection returned "fast-path-v2" but we don't have corresponding runtime.exec spans. Could be log sampling or a race in the traced code path.
maria: dashboard shows KV cache hit-rate stayed flat, so not evictions. throughput dropped ~18% though, so batching math must be off.
linh: I pulled a profiler output from one of the affected hosts, saw kernel fallback loops (fast->fallback->fast) in a tight pattern. Not sure why fallback triggered — no CUDA OOM.
jamal: sounds like a fingerprinting mismatch: selector chooses v2 based on fingerprint, then runtime rejects it because sequence-length estimate differs and triggers fallback. but why missing spans? sampler might be sampling out those exec spans during fallback thrash.
alex: can you paste the profiler stack? I saw increased time in select_kernel() and then in scheduler.yield().
linh: ```
# from perf profiler
select_kernel +0x48  (hot)
scheduler_yield +0x1b
kv_cache_lookup +0x22
runtime_exec_loop +0x7f
```
maria: if select_kernel is hot and we don't emit runtime.exec spans, the tracing guard might be getting bypassed when fallback path is re-entrant. I can repro locally with an artificial fingerprint mismatch.
jamal: repro steps would be great. could be our guard that instruments runtime_exec gets skipped on fast->fallback transition because we short-circuit to fallback path under a spinlock.
alex: can we add a low-overhead event log to the kernel selector (atomic counters) to avoid trace sampling issues? cheap metrics will give us coverage without traces.
linh: I'll add counters: selector_decisions{kernel=fast-v2, outcome=accepted/rejected, reason}. roll a canary to one host.
maria: also increase sampling rate for the selector span for the ramp experiment; right now it's at 0.01 which probably missed the thrash.
jamal: good. action items: 1) linh add selector metrics and deploy canary (ETA 20m). 2) maria bump selector trace sampling to 0.1 for the experiment group (ETA 10m). 3) alex add a short-term dashboard panel showing selector_decisions and kernel_exec_count per host. 4) jamal collect traces for the next ramp window.
linh: deploying canary now to us-west-2 host i-0cafe (rolling). will update when metrics appear.
deploy-bot: deployment started: canary/selector-metrics -> i-0cafe (job 7893).
alex: once metrics show up we should be able to correlate rejected decisions with the CPU spike. If that lines up, we'll patch selector to avoid rapid fallback loops (debounce or require epoch change).
maria: note — the KV cache hit-rate metric has coarse resolution (1m). for micro-bursts it may not reflect transient evictions. we should add a short-window kv_eviction_rate (10s) to catch these.
jamal: agreed. longer term: we need end-to-end guardrails so a bad selector decision doesn't cause fallback thrash and missing traces. short term we'll rely on counters + higher sampling.
linh: metrics visible: selector_decisions appearing now on canary — seeing ~12% rejected with reason="seq_est_mismatch" during spike windows.
ajex: (typo) alex: nice, that's the signal. can we gate the experiment to abort when rejected rate >5%?
maria: yes, implement abort rule in rollout controller. I'll draft a quick rule.
jamal: thanks team. keep monitoring — next ramp scheduled 10:00 UTC. I'll post a follow-up with correlation graphs. :thumbsup:
linh: logging follow-up: I'll also add a tiny always-on text log line for each selector decision so we can't lose visibility even if spans are sampled out (low cardinality).
jamal: perfect. closing loop once we see next ramp results.
